Specifically, p53 triggers apoptosis (removal of damaged cells) and can also induce senescence (permanent cell cycle exit), both of which prevent proliferation of potentially cancerous cells. Therefore, the most accurate options reflecting p53's functions are 'Senescence' and 'Apoptosis'.
